opportunities.title: Synthesis grants

amount.raw: Synthesis groups can claim up to £30,000 over two years for groups of 8-15 participants.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: The main applicant must have BES membership (not required for all group members). Groups must have a diverse mix of members at different career stages, institutions and international participation, and must demonstrate EDI principles and FAIR data principles. Groups of 8-15 individuals, not formed entirely of academic institutions.
opportunities.summary: Funds the formation of new two-year synthesis groups that bring together diverse interdisciplinary groups of 8-15 individuals to focus on data analysis and synthesis, fostering collaboration and mentoring. Groups meet using a hybrid model with two in-person meetings at start and end.

opportunities.title: Long-term research grants

amount.raw: £500 per year for 10 years; first five years' worth of funding (£3,500) claimable in year 1, with an additional £3,500 claimable in year 6 after a satisfactory report.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to all types of ecologists including conservation practitioners, reserve managers, consultants and university academics. Awards are made to individuals, not organisations.
opportunities.summary: Provides a small amount of funding each year for 10 years to enable existing short-term projects with at least 1-2 years of data to be funded into the long term, supporting projects such as ecological restoration, habitat creation, control of alien species and climate change anywhere in the world.

opportunities.title: Pedagogical research and development grants

amount.raw: Projects can be awarded up to £5,000.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Awards are to individuals, not organisations. Open to anyone involved in teaching ecology at any level (early years to lifelong learning, formal or informal settings) and to those in industry exploring the impact of new teaching ideas. Funding unavailable for work forming part of a degree/masters/PhD/fellowship.
opportunities.summary: Funds research informing teaching and learning practices that improve learners' experience and promote excellence in teaching in ecology, including evidence-based examples of innovative practice, systematic reviews, exploring emerging areas of education research, and disseminating best practice.

opportunities.title: Connecting ecologists with other disciplines grants

amount.raw: Grant awards of up to £20,000 can be claimed.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Awards are to individuals, not organisations. Open to PhD students, postdoctoral fellows, early career ecologists, established researchers or employees of other organisations who have employer/supervisor approval and a willing host organisation. Undergraduates and masters students are not eligible.
opportunities.summary: Funds an immersive secondment placement (up to 12 months, full-time or part-time) that immerses an ecologist in another professional world (another discipline, NGO/charity, public sector, business) to develop interdisciplinary skills and foster relationships between disciplines and sectors.

opportunities.title: Small research grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must have BES membership. Open to researchers from all countries globally; projects can be conducted anywhere in the world. Funding is not a scholarship; will not cover principal researcher salary, bench fees or departmental vehicle hire. Requires two reference statements.
opportunities.summary: Supports new and innovative ecological research of the highest international standard, with a clear ecological science focus, for researchers from all countries globally.

opportunities.title: Outreach and engagement grants
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Lead applicant must have BES membership. Open to individuals, teams and organisations across all experience levels. Projects should be a maximum of 12 months. No restrictions on where applicants come from or carry out the work. Aimed at non-academic audiences.
opportunities.summary: Supports BES members to deliver independent outreach, public engagement and science communication activities that engage public audiences with the excitement, importance and relevance of ecological science, in diverse formats such as in-person events, digital formats or physical resources.

opportunities.title: Training and travel grants

amount.raw: A maximum of £250 is available to cover registration fees for virtual conferences/courses; a maximum of £500 is available for events in person.

opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member and a PhD student or postgraduate researcher (postdoc researchers, undergraduates and masters students not eligible). Must work/study at a university or research institution and work in scientific areas within the ecology remit.
opportunities.summary: Helps PhD students and postgraduate researchers meet the costs of specialist field training courses and to network and publicise their research by presenting at workshops and conferences. Awarded on a lottery-based system. Third 2026 round opens 24 August and closes 8 September.

opportunities.title: Annual Meeting Grants 2026
opportunities.eligibility_summary: Must be a BES member at any career stage, a citizen of and based in a Global South country, travelling from and returning to that country, must have applied to present at the Annual Meeting, and must be at least three years since last awarded a BES Training and Travel Grant.
opportunities.summary: Supports researchers based in Global South countries to attend the BES Annual Meeting 2026 in the UK, covering costs directly related to attending the meeting such as registration, transport, food and accommodation. Open 17 July 2026 to 8 September 2026; awarded via lottery.
